memory_update.text: AMKR is a direct public-company mapping to advanced packaging, including WLFO, SiPh, and CPO; should remain a core reference name for the node.
COHR and LITE are the clearest US-listed optical-component exposures for the CPO sub-node, with capacity buildout and AI data-center demand as key verification points.
ALMU belongs in a speculative shadow lane only; it needs commercial evidence before graduating beyond hypothesis status.
Powertech Technology appears highly relevant to the node but is non-US-listed and therefore excluded from the current universe expansion pass.
Need primary-source validation for AI advanced packaging and CPO beneficiary names; current evidence is mostly secondary research snippets, not filings or company disclosures.
Underfollowed lane should prioritize niche photonics and overflow packaging suppliers with customer qualification evidence before broader OSAT names.
AI advanced packaging node appears to extend from packaging overflow into photonics and optical interconnect supply constraints rather than only CoWoS-style packaging.
AMKR should remain the US-listed reference OSAT for the advanced packaging / FOPLP overflow node, but later layers must separate real AI/HPC packaging revenue from generic OSAT exposure.
KLIC is an underfollowed equipment candidate for advanced packaging because bonding / placement accuracy may be a yield gate for fan-out, flip-chip, and thermo-compression bonding flows.
ONTO is a strong process-control candidate for panel-level packaging because its lithography, inspection, metrology, and software map directly to FOPLP yield and RDL process control.

VECO is an underfollowed CPO-adjacent equipment candidate because InP laser, MOCVD, IBD, wet-processing, and optical-interconnect capacity may become upstream bottlenecks as AI systems migrate toward optical I/O.

Need a later search pass for non-US-listed Asian OSATs and FOPLP specialists, including Powertech, ASE, JCET, Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, and packaging material suppliers, because the strongest pure exposure may not be US-listed.

For this node, the highest-value evidence will be customer qualification, advanced-packaging backlog, capex tied to FOPLP or 2.5D/3D, yield milestones, optical-interconnect orders, and AI/HPC revenue disclosure rather than generic packaging language.

AMKR should remain a reference anchor for US-listed advanced packaging/OSAT overflow capacity, but later layers must verify AI/HPC customer mix and capacity qualification rather than assuming all advanced packaging is AI-relevant.
ONTO and ACMR are better underfollowed equipment/process-tool mappings for FOPLP and panel-level packaging than mega-cap semiconductor equipment leaders in this pass.
KLIC is a focused CPO/silicon-photonics bonding-equipment candidate; survival to Layer 2 depends on proving production-scale CPO orders, not only development-tool wins.

Need a follow-up search for US-listed materials and components tied to redistribution layers, temporary bonding/debonding, glass-core substrates, thermal interface materials, and optical-engine attach; current pass is equipment/OSAT-heavy.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: This pass expands the universe for the AI advanced-packaging / CPO node using two lanes: obvious reference leaders for context, and underfollowed public names that may sit on the overflow, materials, optical-device, or packaging integration path. The strongest publicly evidenced names in the supplied context are Amkor, Coherent, and Lumentum, with Aeluma as a smaller, more speculative optics/materials exception. Powertech Technology is highly relevant from the external research snippets, but it is not US-listed, so it is excluded from the candidate list per the task scope. This pass expands the universe around AI advanced packaging and optical integration chokepoints. The strongest context names are TSMC, Broadcom, and NVIDIA as demand anchors, but the more interesting Layer 1B hunt is in underfollowed overflow packaging, panel-level fan-out, substrate/test, and photonics-capacity suppliers. Evidence from recent research snippets points to Powertech Technology as a direct overflow packaging/testing beneficiary with FOPLP and early CPO work, while Aeluma, Coherent, and Lumentum appear in the constrained photonics chain. Most of these claims still need primary-source validation from filings, transcripts, or customer disclosures. Expanded the US-listed universe for the advanced packaging / FOPLP / CPO node using a two-lane funnel. The reference lane keeps one direct OSAT anchor, Amkor, because it maps most directly to advanced packaging overflow and US domestic packaging capacity. The underfollowed lane prioritizes less obvious equipment and process-control chokepoints: Kulick
